summary: Avatar's initials-only sibling: a lit, bevelled disc in one of eight colours, for people with no photo.
useWhen: someone has no profile image and the fallback should still look deliberate rather than empty
a list of people reads better when each one is a different colour — the colour is recognisable long before the letters are legible

useInstead.when: there is a photo, or there may be one later
useInstead.why: Avatar falls back from image to initials to icon on its own; this component has no image to fall back from

useInstead.when: the mark needs a square shape, an icon, a ring or a status indicator
useInstead.why: Figma draws none of those on this component, and a gradient this directional only reads on a circle

useInstead.when: the thing being marked is a status, count or category rather than a person

mini.use: 24px — inline beside body text, dense table rows

slate.use: the default. The one to reach for when nothing about the person suggests a colour

blue.use: as slate — one of seven, picked to tell people apart

pink.use: as slate. See `a11y.knownIssues` before putting it behind text that matters

green.use: as slate. Not a status — a green disc here does not mean online, and Avatar's `bottomIndicator` is what does

red.use: as slate. Not an error — this is identity, not state. See `a11y.knownIssues`

light.use: dark text on a near-white disc, for dense surfaces where seven saturated circles would shout

guarantees: `alt` falls back to `initials`, so the disc is never announced as an unlabelled image
requires: `alt` naming the person — "Ada Lovelace", not "AB". Two letters are not a name, and that is all a screen reader would otherwise get
notes: Colour is decoration here, never information. Nothing about which of the eight a person gets should be recoverable, because a screen reader cannot recover it.

antiPatterns.dont: picking the colour from a status — green for online, red for failing
antiPatterns.do: use Avatar's `bottomIndicator`, or say it in text
antiPatterns.why: the colour is identity, not state. It is also invisible to assistive tech, so a status expressed only this way is not expressed at all

antiPatterns.dont: hashing a user id to a colour and treating it as stable
antiPatterns.do: store the chosen colour with the person, the way you would store their avatar
antiPatterns.why: the palette has eight entries and any hash of it will collide; worse, it silently reassigns everyone the day the palette or the hash changes
Figma draws two. Three fit at 48 and clip at 24, so it looks correct in the story and wrong in the table
